questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

F + 3 = I; I + 3 = L; L + 3 = O

Q + 3 = T; T + 3 = W; W + 3 = Z

P - 1 = O; O + 8 = W; W + 3 = Z

K + 3 = N; N + 3 = Q; Q + 3 =T

Hence, ‘POWZ’ is the odd one out.

questions.question: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statement to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some teachers are philosophers. Some philosophers are writers. Conclusions: I. Some writers are teachers. II. No writer is a teacher.

Some teachers are philosophers.

Some philosophers are writers.

Conclusions:

I. Some writers are teachers.

II. No writer is a teacher.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
options.html: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows
options.html: Either conclusion I or II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

Conclusions:

I. Some writers are teachers → False (It is possible but not definite.)

II. No writer is a teacher → False (It is possible but not definite.)

Both conclusions I and II forms complementary pair.

Hence, either conclusion I or II follows.

questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct? 8 × 2 + 5 - 16 ÷ 4 = 14
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

8 × 2 + 5 - 16 ÷ 4 = 14
questions.solution:
According to BODMAS rule, the sequence of arithmetic operation will be Division, Multiplication, Addition and Subtraction.

8 × 2 ÷ 5 - 16 + 4 is not equal to 14

8 - 2 + 5 × 16 ÷ 4 is not equal to 14

8 ÷ 2 + 5 - 16 × 4 is not equal to 14

8 + 2 × 5 - 16 ÷ 4 is equal to 14

By interchanging x and +, we can make the equation correct.

Hence option 2 is correct.

questions.solution:
Let the present age of Tanya be X.

Given that X = 10

Nisha’s age = 3x

= 3 x 10 = 30

Deepak’s age = 30 + 5 = 35

Deepak‘s age at the time of Tanya’s birth = 35 - 10 = 25

Hence, 25 is the correct answer.

questions.solution: A vestigial organ is a body organ that has lost its function due to evolution. questions.question: What is the name given to the graph that shows all the combinations of two commodities that a consumer can afford at given market prices and within the particular income level in economic terms?
questions.questionHtml: What is the name given to the graph that shows all the combinations of two commodities that a consumer can afford at given market prices and within the particular income level in economic terms?
questions.solution:
• The Budget Line shows all the combinations of two commodities that a consumer can afford at given market prices and within the particular income level in economic terms
  • In other words, the budget line will show how much quantity of two commodities can be bought by consumer if a certain budget is fixed
  • The two constraints in this particular scenario are the fixed budget and the market price of the two goods
  • If there are two goods X and Y, the budget equation can be expressed by Px X Qx +  Py X Qy = M
  • Where Px and Py are prices of X and Y, Qx and Qy are quantities of X and Y and M is the money income (budget) of consumer

questions.question: An economic condition when there is one buyer and many sellers is called ______.
questions.questionHtml: An economic condition when there is one buyer and many sellers is called ______.
questions.solution:
• A monopsony is a market condition where there is a single buyer with many sellers
  • It is in fact a condition which is opposite to that of a monopoly
  • In a monopsony the single buyer has large control on the market as the major purchaser of goods and services provided by many sellers
  • An example would be a food retailer that buys supplies from many farmers growing the same crop

 

Type Description
Oligopoly A market dominated by only a small number of firms
Monopoly A market structure where a single firm controls the entire market
Perfect Competition Market where a large number of small firms compete against each other. In this scenario, a single firm does not have any significant market power

questions.question: If \(\sqrt x - \frac{1}{{\sqrt x }}{\rm{\;}} = {\rm{\;}}4\) , then \({x^2}{\rm{\;}} + {\rm{\;}}\frac{1}{{{x^2}}}\) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\sqrt x - \frac{1}{{\sqrt x }}{\rm{\;}} = {\rm{\;}}4\), then \({x^2}{\rm{\;}} + {\rm{\;}}\frac{1}{{{x^2}}}\) is equal to:
questions.solution:
As we know,

⇒ (x – 1/x)2 = x2 + 1/x2 – 2

Given, √x – 1/√x = 4

⇒ (√x – 1/√x)2 = (√x)2 + (1/√x)2 – 2

⇒ 42 = x + 1/x – 2

⇒ x + 1/x = 16 + 2 = 18

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = x2 + (1/x)2 + 2

⇒ 182 = x2 + 1/x2 + 2

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = 324 – 2 = 322

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, AB is the diameter and CD is a chord such that ABCD is a trapezium. If ∠BAC = 40°, then ∠CAD is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, AB is the diameter and CD is a chord such that ABCD is a trapezium. If ∠BAC = 40°, then ∠CAD is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given, ∠BAC = 40°

⇒ ∠ACB = 90° [angle in a semicircle is 90]

In ΔACB

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠CBA + ∠BAC = 180°

⇒ ∠CBA = 180° – 90° – 40° = 50°

⇒ ∠DCA = ∠CAB = 40° [Alternate interior angle]

⇒ ∠DCA = ∠ABD = 40° and ∠CAD = ∠DBC

∵ Two inscribed angles forming the same arc or forming two equal arcs are equal.

⇒ ∠CBA = ∠DBC + ∠ABD

⇒ 50° = ∠DBC + 40°

⇒ ∠DBC = 50° – 40° = 10°

⇒ ∠CAD = ∠DBC = 10°

questions.solution:
⇒ a : b = 3 : 2

Suppose a = 3 & b = 2

⇒ (5a + 2b) : (3a + 4b)

⇒ (5 × 3 + 2 × 2) : (3 × 3 + 4 × 2)

⇒ ( 15 + 4) : (9 + 8)

⇒ 19 : 17

questions.question: A train without stoppage travels with an average speed of 50 km/h, and with stoppage, it travels with an average speed of 40 km/h. For how many minutes does the train stop on an average per hour?
questions.questionHtml: A train without stoppage travels with an average speed of 50 km/h, and with stoppage, it travels with an average speed of 40 km/h. For how many minutes does the train stop on an average per hour?
questions.solution:
Without stoppage average speed = 50 km/h

With stoppages average speed = 40 km/h

As we know,

Time of rest per hour equal to the difference in average speed divided by the speed without stoppage.

Required time = [(50 – 40)/50] × 60 = 12

So, A train stops on an average 12 minute/hr

questions.question: The radius of a sphere is reduced by 40%. By what percent will its volume decrease?
questions.questionHtml: The radius of a sphere is reduced by 40%. By what percent will its volume decrease?
questions.solution:
Let the radius of sphere be r cm.

Volume of sphere = [4/3] × π r3

If the radius reduced by 40%

New radius of sphere = r × [60/100] = 0.6r

New volume of sphere = [4/3] × π × (0.6r)3 = [4/3] × π × 0.216 × r3

Volume decreased by = \(\frac{4}{3}{\rm{\Pi }}{{\rm{r}}^3} - \frac{4}{3}{\rm{\Pi \;}} \times {\rm{}}0.216{{\rm{r}}^3}{\rm{}} = {\rm{}}\frac{4}{3}{\rm{\Pi }}{{\rm{r}}^3}\left( {1 - 0.216} \right){\rm{}} = {\rm{\;}}0.784{\rm{}} \times {\rm{}}\frac{4}{3}{\rm{\Pi }}{{\rm{r}}^3}\)

Required percentage = \(\left[ {\frac{{0.784{\rm{\;}} \times {\rm{\;}}\frac{4}{3}{\rm{\Pi }}{{\rm{r}}^3}}}{{\frac{4}{3}{\rm{\Pi }}{{\rm{r}}^3}}}} \right]{\rm{}} \times {\rm{}}100\) = 78.4%

questions.question: If a + b + c = 13 and ab + bc + ca = 54, then a 3 + b 3 + c 3 – 3abc is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If a + b + c = 13 and ab + bc + ca = 54, then a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup> + c<sup>3</sup> – 3abc is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given, a + b + c = 13 and ab + bc + ca = 54

As we know,

⇒ a3 + b3 + c3 – 3abc = (a + b + c) [(a + b + c)2 – 3(ab + bc + ca)]

⇒ 13 [132 – 3 × 54]

⇒ 13 (169 – 162)

⇒ 13 × 7

⇒ 91

questions.question: If sec 4θ = cosec (θ + 20°), then θ is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If sec 4θ = cosec (θ + 20°), then θ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

 sec 4θ = cosec (θ + 20°)

Calculation:

sec 4θ = cosec (θ + 20°)

⇒ sec4θ = sec [90° – (θ + 20°)]

⇒ 4θ = 90° – θ – 20°

⇒ 5θ = 70°

⇒ θ = 14°

So, the value of θ is 14°

questions.question: The average marks of 40 students was found to be 68. If the marks of two students were incorrectly entered as 48 and 64 instead of 84 and 46 respectively, then what is the correct average?
questions.questionHtml: The average marks of 40 students was found to be 68. If the marks of two students were incorrectly entered as 48 and 64 instead of 84 and 46 respectively, then what is the correct average?
questions.solution:
Average marks of 40 students = 68

Sum of marks of 48 students = 68 × 40 = 2720

According to the question

Correct sum of marks of 48 students = 2720 – 48 – 64 + 84 + 46 = 2738

Correct average marks of 40 students = 2738/40 = 68.45

questions.question: The price of sugar is increased by 20%. A person wants to increase his expenditure by 8% only. By what percent should he decrease his consumption?
questions.questionHtml: The price of sugar is increased by 20%. A person wants to increase his expenditure by 8% only. By what percent should he decrease his consumption?
questions.solution:
Let the initial price of sugar be 100x.

Price of sugar after increased = 100x × [120/100] = 120x

Person wants his expenditure increase by 8% only, so his expenditure should be = 100x × [108/100] = 108x

∴ Required percentage = (120x – 108x)/120 × 100 = 10%

questions.question: ∆ABC ~ ∆RQP and AB = 4 cm, BC = 6 cm and AC = 5 cm. If ar (∆ABC) : ar (∆PQR) = 9 : 4, Then PQ is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: ∆ABC ~ ∆RQP and AB = 4 cm, BC = 6 cm and AC = 5 cm. If ar (∆ABC) : ar (∆PQR) = 9 : 4, Then PQ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given, AB = 4 cm, BC = 6 cm, AC = 5 cm

If ΔABC ~ ΔRQP

⇒ ar (ΔABC)/ar (ΔPQR) = BC2 / PQ2

⇒ 9/4 = 62/PQ2

⇒ 9/4 = 36/PQ2

⇒ PQ2 = (36 × 4)/9 = 4 × 4

⇒ PQ = 4

questions.question: Two articles are sold for Rs. 9,720 each. On one, the seller gains 8% and on the other, he loses 10%. What is his overall gain or loss?
questions.questionHtml: Two articles are sold for Rs. 9,720 each. On one, the seller gains 8% and on the other, he loses 10%. What is his overall gain or loss?
questions.solution:
SP of each article = Rs. 9720

CP of first article = 9720 × [100/108] = 9000

questions.question: In ∆ABC, AD is the median and G is the centroid point on AD such that AG : GD = 2 : 1. Then ar (∆BDG) : ar (∆ABC) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In ∆ABC, AD is the median and G is the centroid point on AD such that AG : GD = 2 : 1. Then ar (∆BDG) : ar (∆ABC) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Concepts Used:

1. For two triangles, if their base are on the same line and the third vertex is common, then the heights of both triangles become equal

Area(Δ1) : Area(Δ2) = Base1 : Base2

2. Centroid divided the median in the ration 2:1

Calculations:

AD is median, so AD divides the triangle into two equal part

Area (ΔADB) = Area (ΔADC)

In ΔBDG and ΔBGA, the point B is common and their base are on the same line

⇒ Heights (H) of ΔBDG and ΔBGA will be equal

⇒ Area(ΔBDG)/Area(ΔBGA) = [(1/2)DG × H] / [(1/2)AG × H]

⇒ Area(ΔBDG)/Area(ΔBGA) = DG/AG

⇒ Area(ΔBDG)/Area(ΔBGA) = 1/2

Let the Area(ΔBDG) = 1 unit

⇒ Area(ΔBGA) will be = 2 units

Area (ΔBAD) = Area (ΔBDG) + Area (ΔBGA) = 1 + 2 = 3 units

Area (ΔABC) = 2 × Area (ΔBAD) = 2 × 3 = 6 units

⇒ Area (ΔBDG) : Area (ΔABC) = 1 : 6

questions.question: A is 40% more efficient than B and C is 20% less efficient than B. Working together, they can finish a work is 5 days. In how many days will A alone complete 70% of that work?
questions.questionHtml: A is 40% more efficient than B and C is 20% less efficient than B. Working together, they can finish a work is 5 days. In how many days will A alone complete 70% of that work?
questions.solution:
Let efficiency of B be 100

Efficiency of A will be = 100 × [140/100] = 140

Efficiency of C will be = 100 × [80/100] = 80

Efficiency ratio of A, B and C = 140 : 100 : 80 = 7 : 5 : 4

Total work = (7 + 5 + 4) × 5 = 80

70% of total work = 80 × [70/100] = 56

70% of total work A will complete in = 56/7 = 8 days

questions.question: If the six digit number 15x1y2 is divisible by 44, then (x + y) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If the six digit number 15x1y2 is divisible by 44, then (x + y) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Divisibility law of 4: A number divisible by 4 if its last 2 digit is divisible by 4

Divisibility law of 11: If the difference of the alternating sum of digits of the number is a multiple of 11 (e.g. 2343 is divisible by 11 because 2 - 3 + 4 - 3 = 0, which is a multiple of 11).

⇒ 15x1y2 is divisible by 4 if y = 1 or 3

If y = 1, then

⇒ 15x112 is divisible by 11 if x = 6

If y = 3 then

⇒ 15x132 is divisible by 11 If x = 4

If y = 1 and x = 6, then

⇒ x + y = 1 + 6 = 7

If y = 3 and x = 4, then

⇒ x + y = 3 + 4 = 7

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Coming from an affluent family, she found herself a square peg in a round hole when she married a poor farmer and moved to a small village.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

Coming from an affluent family, she found herself a square peg in a round hole when she married a poor farmer and moved to a small village.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "a misfit in the environment."

Key Points

  • The phrase "a square peg in a round hole" contextually implies being in a situation where one does not fit or is not suited to the circumstances.
    • For example: Despite all his skills, he felt like a square peg in a round hole in the finance department.
  • "A misfit in the environment" (पर्यावरण में एक अनुपयुक्त) can be synonymous in this context because both phrases denote a state of not being well-suited or comfortable in a particular setting or situation.
  • Trick: Think of the actual action of attempting to fit a square peg into a round hole – it's not a match. Similarly, being "a square peg in a round hole" is akin to being 'a misfit in the environment,' highlighting an incompatibility or discomfort in adapting, making 'a misfit in the environment' a suitable interpretation.

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. European cloth manufacturers therefore had to depend on a plant called woad to make dyes. B. However, cloth dyers preferred indigo which produced a rich blue colour. C. Being a plant of the temperate zones, woad was easily available in Europe. D. Indian indigo was very expensive and only small quantities reached the European markets.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.

A. European cloth manufacturers therefore had to depend on a plant called woad to make dyes.

B. However, cloth dyers preferred indigo which produced a rich blue colour.

C. Being a plant of the temperate zones, woad was easily available in Europe.

D. Indian indigo was very expensive and only small quantities reached the European markets.
questions.solution:
The first sentence of the passage introduces the topic of the passage and stands independently in meaning. This is only true for sentence D. The other sentences all refer to concepts not mentioned within them.

Hence, sentence D is the first sentence.

The next sentence should be A since it mentions the word therefore describing how cloth manufacturers had to depend on something. Therefore, the previous sentence must mention a reason for this, which is true for sentence D that states that indigo was expensive.

The next sentence will be C, since it expands further on the topic of woad mentioned in the previous sentence, A.

Finally, the last sentence will be B.

Therefore, the correct order of sentences is DACB.

Hence, option 2 is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement. Biologists believe that increased human activity means an accelerated rate of change in habitat for all creatures of the world.

Biologists believe that increased human activity means an accelerated rate of change in habitat for all creatures of the world.

options.text: human activities mean an acelerated rate from change

questions.solution:
The given sentence is grammatically correct and requires no change. Here are the reasons why:

  • Human activity is a singular noun and requires a verb in its singular form. Hence, the verb form means fits here.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.solution:
When describing the quality of an action performed by someone, we use the words act of followed by a noun that describes that quality. 

For example:

  • An act of cruelty
  • An act of bravery
     

Therefore, in the given context, the correct preposition to be used should be of to describe telling someone something that you admire about them as an act of kindness i.e. a kind act. 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.solution:
The correct word here should be effort.

The context of the given sentence clearly states that complimenting someone pays enormous dividends despite requiring almost no activity or attempt from one's side.

Replacing effort with any of the other options - venture, knowledge and result would not make the same sense.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.
questions.solution:
The correct verb form to fit in the blank here is simple present tense form spend. 

This is because the sentence is making a general statement that applies to the lives of 'many people', both in the past and present. Hence, the past tense forms in options 1 and 3 don't make sense.

Option 4 is in the present perfect continuous tense (have been spending) and does not fit here either because it denotes an action that started in the past and has continued up to the present moment.

Simple present tense (spend), on the other hand, is used to talk about things that happen regularly.

Hence, option 2 is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4
questions.solution:
Here are the meanings of the given words:

  • Acknowledge - to recognise the importance or quality of something or someone
  • Admit - to confess to be true
  • Concede - to admit, often unwillingly, that something is true
  • Confess - to admit that you have done something wrong

 

The given passage clearly talks about the kindness of telling people what you admire about them. Out of the given words, clearly acknowledge best expresses this meaning.

Hence, option 1 is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.5.
questions.solution:
The correct word that fits the blank here is however.

This is because this word helps us make a contrast between the previous part of the sentence (that we like compliments from friends and family) and the next one (that compliments from strangers can also feel good if they are genuine). 

Because and so express a cause and effect relationship. Unless is used to mean except. None of these options help make contextual sense of the sentence.

Therefore, option 4 is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. AFFINITY
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

AFFINITY
questions.solution:
The word affinity means a liking or sympathy for someone or something.

Here are the meanings of all the given options:

  • Aversion -  a feeling of strong dislike or of not wishing to do something
  • Preference - the fact that you like something or someone more than another thing
  • Attraction - a feeling of liking someone
  • Empathy- the capacity to understand or feel what another person is experiencing

 

Out of the given words, we can see that the word aversion is completely opposite to the meaning of the word affinity.

In fact, the other options are synonyms of the given word.

Hence, option 1 is correct.

The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. reflective.

Key Points

  • The word "pensive" means engaged in, involving, or reflecting deep or serious thought. (विचारमग्न)
    • Example: She sat by the window in a pensive mood, thinking about her future.
  • "Reflective" refers to someone who is given to or marked by deep thought; thoughtful. (चिंतनशील)
    • Example: After the meeting, he became reflective, pondering over the decisions he had made.
  • Hence, we can infer that the synonym of 'pensive' is 'reflective'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. reflective.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Tragic (दुखद): Causing or characterized by extreme distress or sorrow.
    • Example: The tragic news of the accident left everyone in shock.
  • Spontaneous (स्वतःस्फूर्त): Performed or occurring as a result of a sudden inner impulse without premeditation.
    • Example: His spontaneous laughter was infectious and made everyone around him laugh too.
  • Spiteful (द्वेषपूर्ण): Showing or caused by malice; hateful.
    • Example: She made a spiteful remark to hurt his feelings intentionally.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. ACCEPT
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

ACCEPT
questions.solution:
The word accept means to say yes or to agree to take something.

Out of the given options, only reject is completely opposite in meaning to the given word as it means to refuse to accept, use, or believe something or someone.

Hence, option 3 is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement. A reason why there are so much misconception on dyslexia could be the sheer invisibility of the disorder.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement.

A reason why there are so much misconception on dyslexia could be the sheer invisibility of the disorder.

options.text: there are so many misconceptions about dyslexia
options.html: there are so many misconceptions about dyslexia

options.text: there are so many misconception around dyslexia
options.html: there are so many misconception around dyslexia

options.text: there are so much misconceptions against dyslexia
options.html: there are so much misconceptions against dyslexia

questions.solution:
The word misconception means a belief or an idea that is not based on correct information, or that is not understood by people. When used in this context, it is a countable noun.

  • For example: There are several common misconceptions about the theory of relativity. 
     

Note that the word is in its plural form above. Hence, the given sentence and option 2 cannot be correct.

Since it is a countable noun, we cannot use words such as so much to quantify the word. 

The only option that accurately represents the correct usage of the word misconception is option 1.

Hence, option 1 is correct.

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. No sooner did he see the tiger when he ran as fast as he could.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

No sooner did he see the tiger when he ran as fast as he could.
questions.solution:
The construction no sooner...than is used to represent a situation in which the second event occurs immediately after the first.

For example: No sooner had the teacher left the classroom than the children started to scream.

The use of when in the given sentence is, therefore, incorrect.

Hence, the error is in the part of the sentence in option 1.

questions.question: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Something which is fit to be eaten
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.

Something which is fit to be eaten
questions.solution:
Out of the given options, tasty and delicious are commonly known words that mean pleasant to the taste.

Here are the meanings of the other two options:

  • Edible - fit to be eaten
  • Unpalatable - unpleasant to taste or eat

 

Out of these, edible clearly fits the meaning of the words provided. 

For example: He might not be a great cook, but at least his food is edible.

Hence, option 1 is correct.

questions.question: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The match is about to begin since the captain as well as the team are on the field.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

The match is about to begin since the captain as well as the team are on the field.

options.text: The match is about to begin
options.html: The match is about to begin

questions.solution:
The construction as well as is used to conjoin two expressions, but it cannot be used in the way that we use and. It is used to add an expression with the first one but not to combine them together.

For example, we say: 'My mother and father are coming to the party'. (The subject becomes plural)

But when we use as well as we say: 'My mother, as well as my father, is coming to the party.'  (The subject my mother remains singular)

Therefore, in the given sentence, it is inaccurate to use the plural verb form are since the subject of the verb is the captain i.e. singular.

Hence, the error is in the part of the sentence in option 1.

questions.question: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Something which cannot be understood
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.

Something which cannot be understood
questions.solution:
Here are the meanings of all the given options:

  • Incomprehensible -  impossible to understand or comprehend
  • Infallible - never wrong, failing, or making a mistake
  • Illegible - not clear enough to be read
  • Inexplicable -  incapable of being explained or interpreted

 

Out of the given words, we can see that only the word incomprehensible fits the meaning of the given words.

Hence, option 1 is correct.

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Here, the picture perfect French Quarter and heritage laden Tamil streets blend into one another. B. The conflict of coexistence is evident in many metropolitan cities. C. The old and new, like two different worlds, surviving side by side yet never crossing that chasm. D. There is a place though, Puducherry, where contrasts are celebrated like nowhere else.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.

A. Here, the picture perfect French Quarter and heritage laden Tamil streets blend into one another.

B. The conflict of coexistence is evident in many metropolitan cities.

C. The old and new, like two different worlds, surviving side by side yet never crossing that chasm.

D. There is a place though, Puducherry, where contrasts are celebrated like nowhere else.
questions.solution:
The first sentence of the passage introduces the theme or topic of the passage and stands independently in meaning. This is only true for sentence B. The other sentences all either elaborate on another topic or refer to concepts not mentioned within them.

Hence, sentence B is the first sentence.

The next sentence will be D since it offers an example (Puducherry) as well as direct a point of contrast (There is a place though) from the idea discussed in B. 

The next sentence will be A. It directly expands on the topic of Puducherry that was first mentioned in the previous sentence.

The last sentence should be C since it elaborates on the theme of conflict of coexistence introduced in sentence B.

Therefore, the correct order of sentences is BDAC.

Hence, option 2 is correct.

questions.question: Select the correct active form of the given sentence. Let the bell be rung every forty minutes.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

Let the bell be rung every forty minutes.

options.text: Ring the bell every forty minutes.
options.html: Ring the bell every forty minutes.

options.text: The bell ought to be rung every forty minutes.
options.html: The bell ought to be rung every forty minutes.

options.text: The bell should be rung every forty minutes.
options.html: The bell should be rung every forty minutes.

options.text: Let the bell keep ringing every forty minutes.
options.html: Let the bell keep ringing every forty minutes.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ring the bell every forty minutes.

Here's why:

The given sentence is an imperative sentence in the passive voice. A sentence that expresses a wish, command or request is called an imperative sentence.

In order to change an imperative sentence from passive to active voice, we must:

  • Drop the word let.
  • Use the present form (ring) of the word in an active instead of the past participle (rung) in passive.
  • Drop the word be'

 

Only the sentence in option 1 follows these rules.

Hence, option 1 is correct.

questions.question: Directions: In this section each of the following sentences has a blank space and each sentence is followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill the blank space. Technology can be ______ and people seem to be more attached to screens than ever before.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: In this section each of the following sentences has a blank space and each sentence is followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill the blank space.

Technology can be ______ and people seem to be more attached to screens than ever before.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (1) i.e. "addictive".

Key Points 

  • Here are the meanings of all the given options:
  • Addictive-  an activity or substance likely to get someone unhealthily attached or obsessed with it(ऐसी गतिविधि या पदार्थ जिसके प्रति किसी का अस्वस्थ रूप से जुड़ाव या जुनून होने की संभावना हो)
  • Contagious - (of a disease) spread from one person or organism to another((किसी बीमारी का) एक व्यक्ति या जीव से दूसरे व्यक्ति में फैलना)
  • Infatuated - having a very strong but not usually lasting feeling of love or attraction towards someone(किसी के प्रति प्यार या आकर्षण की बहुत मजबूत लेकिन आमतौर पर स्थायी नहीं होने वाली भावना होना)
  • Incorrigible - incapable of being corrected or amended(सुधार या संशोधन करने में असमर्थ)

In the context of the sentence, technology is described as something that people seem likely to get irrationally attached to. Hence, of all the given options, it can best be described as addictive.

Therefore, option 1 is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. People of the older generation ______ over the good old school days.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

People of the older generation ______ over the good old school days.
questions.solution:
From the context of the sentence, we see that the word in the blank needs to be combined with the preposition over to convey a meaning of longingly thinking about past experiences.

The words remember and remind can't be combined with over to convey this meaning.

The word retribute means to pay back or give in return and hence is contextually wrong.

The word reminisces, however, can be combined with the preposition over to mean indulge in enjoyable recollections of past events.

  1. Retribute - प्रतिकार करना
  2. Reminisce - याद करना
  3. Remind - याद दिलाना
  4. Remember - याद रखना

Hence, option 2 is correct.
